summary: The bill makes permanent the additional standard deduction for seniors by amending the tax code to remove its expiration after 2028, effective for tax years after 2026.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the tax code to make a senior deduction permanent. It has no provisions that authorize, increase, or decrease any form of government outlays or appropriations. Tax revenue effects are distinct from direct spending.

The sole purpose of the bill is to amend IRC Section 151(d)(5)(C)(i) to make the deduction for seniors permanent rather than expiring after 2028. This directly reduces taxable income for qualifying seniors and therefore constitutes a tax cut.
No provisions address health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, provider payments, or any aspect of the healthcare system.
The bill contains no language related to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No references to visas, border security, asylum, or immigration enforcement appear in the text.
The legislation does not mention reproductive health services, funding restrictions, or abortion access.
No defense authorizations, troop levels, or military spending changes are included.
The bill is silent on environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation programs.
While the deduction benefits seniors, the bill does not alter eligibility, benefit levels, or funding for Social Security, Medicare, SSI, or other welfare programs.
No education funding, school choice provisions, or federal education policy changes are present.
The text does not address drug scheduling, enforcement, decriminalization, or treatment programs.
No sentencing guidelines, policing reforms, or incarceration provisions exist.
The bill contains no tariff, trade agreement, or import/export language.

By permanently extending a tax deduction, the bill reduces future federal revenue without any offsetting spending cuts. This modestly increases projected deficits, moving slightly away from debt-reduction priority.
No civil rights, nondiscrimination, or LGBTQ-specific legal protections are addressed.
The legislation does not authorize, modify, or eliminate any foreign assistance programs.
No voting procedures, election administration, or campaign finance provisions are included.
The bill does not regulate technology companies, data collection, or privacy standards.
No labor law, collective bargaining, or union-related measures appear.
The text contains no religious exemptions, conscience clauses, or civil rights balancing provisions.
